Different follow-up modalities may play a role in the diagnosis of asymptomatic endometrial cancer relapses. The optimal approach for identifying and managing relapse is not yet established, and prospective cost-effectiveness studies are needed to inform guideline development.

In one study, researchers found that women with asymptomatic recurrence had better clinical outcomes compared to those with symptomatic relapse. However, they also noted that guidelines comparing follow-up protocols have not been established. As a result, the best approach for managing asymptomatic endometrial cancer relapses remains unclear.

Another study suggested that follow-up after endometrial cancer treatment varies significantly in Italy. The study found that women who underwent immediate surgery had better outcomes compared to those who received only observation or monitoring.

Furthermore, one report indicated that uterine natural killer cells may play a role in regulating cytokines and influencing the development of irregular bleeding in postmenopausal endometrium users of menopausal hormone therapy (HT). This suggests that follow-up after HT treatment might be necessary to monitor for potential side effects.

Additionally, imaging techniques such as diffusion-weighted MR imaging may help detect cancer in patients with nonenhanced MR images. However, the study found that DW imaging can also be useful in identifying uterine endometrial cancer in patients who have undergone nonenhancement MRI.

The findings of these studies highlight the need for further research to determine the most effective follow-up strategies for asymptomatic endometrial cancer relapses.
